notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit Update
notes.content:
We’re pleased to announce the release of version 2.0.22 of the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit.

The changelist is as follows:[list]
[*]Meshes can be combined to create new Entities.
[*]Added an Event Condition Definition, which can be used to create groups of event conditions (such as 'Control Left' and 'Control Up') which must all be met before an Action is triggered.
[*]Actions support Event Conditions, allowing actions based on multiple event criteria.
[*]Added select button to Front-End and HUD editors (lists items in the main page or currently editing popup)
[*]Selecting overlapping items will cycle through them in the Front-End and HUD editors.
[*]Updated the EULA to allow use of the graphics and audio assets within any games (commercial or non-commercial) created with the Shoot 'Em Up Kit.
[*]Added more tooltip help around the Editors.
[*]Fixed an issue that could prevent some Action properties from being saved.
[*]The ‘Back’ option moved to top of list of games in Play window
[*]Project name field has focus when project window opens when creating a project
[*]Displaying a warning if name already used when creating a project
[*]Many small fixes and improvements.
[/list]
We apologise for the long time between updates.  As we’ve posted previously, we’re working on some major low-level engine improvements to update the graphics and audio technologies we use and open up many new possibilities for the future.  However, this has taken longer than planned so we have moved some of the new features from the newer engine into the current one for this release.  This way everyone can start to use them while we continue to update the engine.  This is still on-going and we'll be updating the build with few more features over the next week or two.

Anyway, we hope you enjoy the new features.  The ability to combine meshes is a fun way to create complex objects by joining parts together.  This will take on a new level in our next update when we’ll be including hundreds of new block pieces to play with.

The Event Condition feature gives a more powerful way of controlling which Actions are triggered.  This can be used to trigger an action when the player moves up on the controller and presses fire, for example.

We’ve added some improvements to the Front-End and HUD Editors, and have more plans to improve the functionality and usability of these editors.

We’ve had quite a bit of feedback on the tutorials, particularly the age of the tutorial videos.  Our focus has been on the Wiki, which has quite a lot of content now.  But we will create new video tutorials, as we know some people prefer this method of learning.  And we will replace the old content with videos using the current version of the engine.

We wish you all the very best for 2021 and thank you again for your support.

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone, we hope you are all keeping safe and well.

We wanted to update you on the progress of the Shoot 'Em Up Kit as we shared some new features with you in August and have not yet released a new build.

The new features have been held up by a major upgrade to the low-level engine, which the Kit uses for drawing sprites, models, audio, video, etc, that we've been working on for some time.  We'd hoped and expected to have this finished in August but, despite the Kit working well with the new engine, there are still a lot of tasks which need completing.

We're very aware people are waiting for some of the new features we've been sharing and so we are going to move those over to the existing engine.  We can then work on finishing the new engine without holding up the new features.

We'll get these features moved across as soon as we can and look forward to sharing the new build with you all.

Thank you all for your patience and support.

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit - August Update
notes.content:
Welcome to the August news update of the Shoot 'Em Up Kit.  It has been a while since our last update and we apologise for this.

We've been hard at work on a new graphics engine to use more modern visual effects and gain huge performance benefits in 3D games.  This has been going very well and we are in the last stages of this feature at the moment.

We also welcome Matt to the team.  Matt has been replacing the rotation systems to fix some bugs and allow full Six degrees of freedom rotation for cockpit based flight.

We're also upgrading the version of PhysX used within the Shoot 'Em Up Kit to improve collisions and physics simulations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/c7ae979632a78fe51b4bc95598ef2deb841e1dbb.png[/img]

We've updated the [url=tallstudios.com]Tall Studios[/url] and [url=shootemupkit.com]Shoot 'Em Up Kit[/url] websites.  The Shoot 'Em Up Kit website is now home for the Wiki and tutorials.

We have also been quietly releasing updates to the Shoot 'Em Up Kit which contain bug fixes and optimisations, and we will continue to do this over the next few weeks until the new engine is available.
Once the new engine is ready we can release some new features including UI updates, a more modular and flexible event system, and model building from components.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/77ff0a5ac6cdf167b430c9d2a7ab00e40817f1b8.png[/img]

Thank you for your patience as we put together this major update and we look forward to sharing some exciting new features with you very soon.

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit - April Update
notes.content:
Hello and thank you for checking out our April update for the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit.

[h2]Shoot ‘Em Up Kit version 2.0.20[/h2]
We’re pleased to announce that version 2.0.20 of the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit has been released.  This is mostly a bug fix update but also contains some useful performance improvements and improved collision detection.

The changelist is as follows:
[h3]Version 2.0.20[/h3][list]
[*] Improved project load times.
[*] Improved game logging in debug mode.
[*] Fixed an issue with the score not working correctly if testing level 2 or greater.
[*] Fixed a problem with billboard sprites not facing the camera.
[*] Lights can be attached to tags.
[*] Fixed some problems with formating on the Action tab.
[*] Items can bounce off shields.
[*] The particle collision group now saves correctly.
[*] HUD can now show properties for all players.
[*] The movement definition can be reset.
[*] Fixed some problems with assets appearing in the wrong level.
[*] NPC Generators are correctly duplicated when copying a map.
[*] Fixed a problem where lights could affect other levels.
[*] Many small fixes and improvements.
[/list]
[h2]Multiplatform[/h2]
The Shoot 'Em Up Kit is working well on our new multiplatform engine.  The physics system is now integrated into the engine and all the sample projects and templates are working correctly.  The new engine will allow significant performance and stability improvements on the PC; and will also pave the way for exporting games onto other devices and platforms.

[h2]Model Builder[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/c8488db78ce4c9538a5a3c460b1dd819c9aaf075.gif[/img]
Work is well underway on a new feature that will allow assets to be built from components.  This makes it easy to create custom models in a range of styles.  All of this is done from within the Entity Editor and so your new models are ready to be dropped in-game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/6afe732f7d00999d4a4deb4b3172026a401bdac4.jpg[/img]  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/526b391f28720677abea852fc5eb428f2d17f863.jpg[/img]

[h2]Discord Server[/h2]
The Shoot 'Em Up Kit Discord server is a great place for questions, suggestions or to meet with other members of the community.  You can join us [url=https://discord.gg/G66Z2PZ]here[/url].


Many thanks,
The Tall Studios team

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit - January Update
notes.content:
Welcome to the January update for the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit.  We hope you had a great festive holiday and we wish you all a very happy new year.
[h3]Version 2.0.19[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/b4cd53eaec86cef9381e06bca2ed4132a5097906.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/5960090936bb9867462e93e9ab919831d7782b49.png[/img]

We’re pleased to announce that the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit version 2.0.19 has been released.  This includes many fixes and features including template games, which you can use as a starting point for your own projects; and orthographic cameras to use 3D models without perspective – which is perfect for retro-style games.

[b]Version 2.0.19 Release Notes[/b]
- New projects can be created from a template.
- Created template projects for side-scroller; vertical-scroller; twin-stick shooter; asteroids; top-down; and invaders style games.
- Tutorials have been created for all template games describing how they were built.
- Added an orthographic option to Camerashots.  The orthographic view is only active in-game.
- Added a zoom value to orthographic camera to control the distance to the scene.  Higher values make the scene closer.
- Testing a game or level with the Level Settings window open will automatically apply the current values in the level settings.
- Fixed an issue with shadows appearing brighter than they should.
- Fixed an issue with spotlights not fading in intensity.
- The 'Stop' collision action now works correctly.
- Default Input and Movement Definitions are added to new items placed.
- Timers are reset (if required) when the Player respawns.
- Fixed some issues with level copying.
- Fixed an issue that could cause copied items not to be named in sequence.
- Fixed a controller issue that could prevent twin stick input from working correctly.
- Fixed issues with procedural background settings not working correctly.
- Boolean variables are now shown in debug mode.
- Fixed an issue where changing the scale didn't affect the sprite in the Entity Editor.
- Tag positions are automatically adjusted when a sprite is scaled in the Entity Editor.
- Fixed an issue that prevented loading an autosave.
- Fixed an issue that could fire two bullets when the analogue stick was at specific angles.
- Items can now be pasted in the level when the Definition Editor is open; but not while the Definition Properties window is open.
- Bullet Patterns are now correctly reset when the level restarts.
- Fixed an issue that could allow the Player or NPC to fire after all weapons had been removed.
- Projects saved using "Save As" will appear in the recent project list.
- Flat square entities have a box collision type to match their dimensions.
- Fixed some potential crashes.

[h3]Discord[/h3]
The Shoot ‘Em Up Kit channel on Discord has been revamped and updated, thanks to SpaghettiLord1010.  Please drop by and say Hello.  https://discord.gg/cCf54z5

[h3]Wiki[/h3]
The wiki pages have been updated for the latest Shoot ‘Em Up Kit update.  There are descriptions of the templates as well as full tutorials going step-by-step through how they were created.
We’re continuing to focus on creating content for the wiki pages.  Thank you to everyone who has requested tutorials.  If there is a tutorial you’d like to see then please let us know.

[h3]Website[/h3]
We will shortly be updating the Tall Studios website, which is long overdue.  We are splitting the company website and the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit product pages so that each may become more focused.

We are archiving the Tall Studios forums on the website as they are rarely used and there are options of contacting us via Discord; Steam Forums; Facebook; Twitter; or email via the website.

Many thanks,
The Tall Studios team

notes.title: Update - November 2019
notes.content:
Hello and thank you for checking out our November update for the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit.
It has been a few months since the version 2.0.18 build was released and so we’d like to share our progress as we move towards the next release.

[h1]Template Games[/h1]
We've been using the Shoot 'Em Up Kit to create some template games and new demos.  These cover some of the common styles of shoot ‘em up: the side-scroller; vertical shooter; twin-stick; invaders; asteroids; and free roaming.
We’re retiring the Wizard feature as this was complex to use and didn’t give the helpful starting point that the templates provide.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/83f7bd000eba3cd756b12f9a577bcd5bbbfeb0a7.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/160ce895fb260db2110ebc7fe98aaa59af7f1672.gif[/img]

[h1]Orthographic Cameras[/h1]
We’re pleased to say that orthographic cameras are now working and so you can create games without the perspective warping at the edges of the screen.  The sprite-only project configuration is still available as this is a useful way of building games using screen pixel co-ordinates.

[h1]Engine Tech[/h1]
We’ve made a lot of improvements to the codebase to improve the stability of the Shoot ‘Em Up Kit when unexpected things happen.  We’ve also improved the use of threading to make the Kit run faster and smoother on modern systems.

[h1]Multi-platform[/h1]
The Shoot 'Em Up Kit is working well on our new multi-platform engine.  There is still a bit of work left to do on the physics and audio but we're very close now.  The new engine will allow significant performance and stability improvements on the PC; and will also pave the way for exporting games onto other devices and platforms.

[h1]Tutorials[/h1]
There are new wiki guides for creating different styles of shoot 'em up.  These describe all the steps involved in creating each of the template games.  We will continue to create these for each of the templates and concept demos.

[h1]Art[/h1]
We are continuing to build a library of components that can be joined together to create new and interesting ships, scenery or collectibles.  You can combine these with your own assets to easily create entities that can be used in your game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/2a4541c7cb092cc9b04581e2e96753a1572caa18.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8977518/431cf66a13d7297540f8d9e0e4d25af5e6641a8e.png[/img]

Many thanks,
The Tall Studios team

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit Update
notes.content:
We're pleased to announce that version 2.0.18 of the Shoot 'Em Up Kit is now available.
This is the biggest update we have released and includes a re-written level editor; support for orthographic 2D games; and a more modular approach to game creation which expands the features and possibilities.
We have created an [url=http://tallstudios.com/wiki/index.php?title=Upgrading_to_Version_2.0.18]Upgrade Wiki page[/url] which explains about the changes introduced in version 2.0.18.  
We recommend that you back up your projects before updating as existing projects will be automatically converted to the new format.  In some cases it may be necessary to make a few changes to your project but the Wiki page explains the steps that may be required.  If you need any help updating your project to version 2.0.18 then please let us know and we will be happy to assist you.
The [url=http://tallstudios.com/wiki/index.php?title=Shoot_%27Em_Up_Kit]Wiki[/url] has been revised for the new version and is replacing the pdf user guide.

The release notes are as follows:
[list]
[*] New Level Editor offers a wide range of improvements.
[*] Multiple items can be selected and moved.
[*] Undo system has been improved for the Level Editor.
[*] Added a fully 2D mode (orthographic mode) for sprite based games.  Zoom features are available in this mode and Layers are restricted from -1 to 3.
[*] Added more Action events.  Each object type (Player, Timer, Spline, etc) has its own set of Action events.
[*] Added Action events for Custom Variables.  Actions can be triggered when a Custom Variable is greater than, less than or equal to a specified value.
[*] Some Actions can be set to only apply to specific collision groups.  
[*] Items can be spawned from an Action.
[*] Custom variables and game properties can be set or modified from Actions.
[*] Collision Groups have options to set whether collision Actions or Events are triggered, damage is taken, or the objects can intersect/overlap.
[*] Items can be set to only become active once they have a parent.  This is useful for weapon pick-ups.
[*] Player and NPC items can both have input controls assigned to them.
[*] NPCs can use shields.
[*] NPCs now support invulnerability time.
[*] Added an Input Definition type.  The input properties have been removed from the Player Definition and added to the new Input Definition.  This allows other objects (e.g. NPCs) to receive input from the player.
[*] Added a Movement Definition type.  The movement properties have been removed from the Player and NPC Definitions and added to the new Movements Definition.
[*] Added AI Events.  AI Behaviours will be notified of these events and can react with a state change.
[*] Weapons are shown own a new Tab.
[*] The Bullet collision type is now set in the Weapon tab rather than the Bullet Definition.  This makes it easier to share weapons and bullets between Player and NPC items.
[*] Particle system supports text.  Particles can be set-up to show Score, Damage or Multiplier values too.
[*] Added Follow Spline Shape AI type.  This will follow the shape of a spline from an Entity's current location rather than travelling to the actual spline (which is still possible with Follow Spline AI type).
[*] Gizmos can use local rotations.  This allows objects to be moved based on the directions they are facing.
[*] Added Camera styles into the Project Settings.  The options are: 3D, 2D with models (sometimes referred to as 2.5D) and 2D with Sprites (sometimes referred to as orthographic).
[*] Shields support collision groups.  Only the specified collision groups will be protected by the shield.
[*] Added ship selection.  Multiple ships can be placed in a level and the player can select a ship from the front-end pages.
[*] Triggers can use screen co-ordinates rather than level co-ordinates.  The trigger will be activated when an object enters the trigger's screen area.
[*] Custom Variables and AI Events may now be created and edited using the Def Tools menu.
[*] In the Front-End and HUD editors, each click on overlapping objects will cycle through the objects.
[*] The Chase, MatchX, MatchY and MatchZ AI behaviours can now use a proximity parameter.  They will only Chase, etc, when within proximity of the target.
[*] Added a 'Follow' AI behaviour.  This will follow its target, staying within a specified distance.
[*] Added a new Action to return the Entity back to its spawn point.
[*] The Attach and Detach Actions support Tags; and detached items can be dropped, destroyed or returned to their spawn point.
[*] Fixed a potential crash when selecting to edit a pop-up.
[*] Snap to Object now works correctly when objects are rotated.
[*] The name and value of Custom Variables are shown on-screen in Debug mode.
[*] Level specific buttons and windows are hidden or disabled until a level has been chosen.
[*] Definitions can have longer names.  Names up to 64 characters in length are supported.
[*] The Movement Def contains an option to turn an Entity to face the direction it is travelling.  This is particularly useful for axis-based movement when you want the Entity to visually rotate.
[*] Rotate Yaw/Pitch/Roll will do a local rotation (rotate around its center point) if the Entity is using axis-based movement.  This allows a visual rotation even when the Entity is set to move along axis.
[*] Added input options to set the rotation direction and move in that direction.  This can be assigned to the Left Analog, Right Analog or Dpad.  There are also options for setting the direction and applying thrust or an impulse.
[*] Many small fixes and improvements.
[/list]
We are continuing to add Wiki pages to provide a full set of tutorials and reference material.  A new set of template games will also be available next week.  We will make an announcement about this as soon as they're ready.

We really hope you enjoy the features in this new version and we thank you for your support.
The Tall Studios Team

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit 2.0.17
notes.content:
We're please to announce that the latest version of the Shoot 'Em Up Kit is now available.

The change list is as follows:

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit 2.0.15
notes.content:
We're pleased to announce that the latest version (2.0.15) of the Shoot 'Em Up Kit is now available.

Here is the changelist for 2.0.15:
[list]
[*] New User Interface.
[*] Particle Editor supports multiple layers of effects.
[*] Added support for AI States.
[*] Added Teleport options for AI Behaviours.
[*] Level Editor supports layers to easily add items at different depths.  Select the layer in the Tools pane or use the PageUp/PageDown shortcuts.
[*] Sprites can be set for different directions.  These will be used when the sprite is rotated in that direction.
[*] Added support for minimum shield duration and shield cooldown.
[*] Added 'Step' movement type.  This causes Entities to jump along their path in steps.  This is useful for retro gaming effects.
[*] Rotation can be set for each NPC Generator node.
[*] Weapon properties 'Reload Time Remaining' and 'Unlimited Ammo' are now accessible to the HUD and Behaviour Editor.
[*] The Player Shield is now saving correctly.
[*] Shield recharge is now working.
[*] A shield button can now be assigned and the shield will only be active once the button is pressed.
[*] An Explorer window is opened at the appropriate directory once a package build has completed.
[*] Fixed problems with some of the AI movement behaviours not using the correct direction.
[*] Camera Roll axis is now fixed.
[*] When placing an object the camera zoom will stop if going through the object.
[*] When placing an object the camera will move back if the current layer is behind the camera.
[*] When Refill All Ammo Clips is selected it will also refill the main ammo level too.
[*] The events for MovingX, MovingY and MovingZ are now triggered correctly.
[*] All effects for the Destroyed event are now triggered correctly.
[*] Fixed a problem that could prevent bullet sprites from looping.
[*] Fixed a problem that could prevent generated NPCs from spawning with the correct rotation.
[*] Improved Spline following.
[*] Fixed an issue that could cause NPCs to ignore their AI behaviour if previous AI types had been deleted.
[*] Rotation offset effect now works correctly.
[*] Removed coloured lines which appeared when an item was selected with the mouse on a front-end page.
[*] Fixed an issue that could result in a sprite being saved without its texture.
[*] Fixed a problem selecting Behaviours in multi-level projects.
[*] Fixed a problem with Behaviours not being correctly triggered in multi-level projects.
[*] Behaviours are correctly copied when a level is copied in the Level Editor.
[*] Fixed an issue with deleting Behaviour Editor nodes that could cause an extra node to be removed too.
[*] Improved particle rotation and velocity interpolation.
[*] Optimisation: Fewer memory allocations.
[*] Optimisation: Test Game and Test Level will start faster.
[/list]

We've added a range of new features but we've also added more depth to some existing features such as the AI, Shield and Particles.

Usability remains an important focus and we have made a lot of tweaks and fixes.  We've also added better support for making levels with items at different depths.

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit 2.0.13
notes.content:
We're pleased to announce the release of Shoot 'Em Up Kit version 2.0.13.

The change list includes:
[list]
[*] It is now possible to create many more front-end pages.
[*] The flow of front-end pages can be customised.  The next page can be set for input and timeout events.
[*] Levels can have their own specific front-end pages that can be triggered before and after the level.
[*] Front-End text and sprites can be set to start the game at a specific level.
[*] Front-End text and sprites can set the value of a user variable.
[*] Fixed an issue that could disable NPCs when moving between full-screen and windowed in-game.
[*] Particle trail time can be less than 1 second.
[*] New sprites are automatically scaled down to 10% of their size in the level editor.  This resizes them to the scale of the 3D environment.
[*] Corrected some inconsistent naming between windows and tabs.
[*] Fixed an issue where the 'Looped' checkbox wasn't set consistently across Sprite Frames.
[*] Particle keyframes can be deleted.
[*] The rotation speed multiplier now defaults to 1.  Previously, the zero value was preventing the AI Entity from rotating.
[*] Fixed an issue with Actions triggering at the start of the level.
[*] Generated NPCs can use formations.
[*] Fixed an issue which prevented the selection of a spline from a formation.
[*] When two objects collide damage is still applied regardless of the Collision Action setting.
[*] Improved the use of multiple CPU cores to optimise the Kit and the games it creates.
[*] Fixed an issue with Action pane not being fully reset when selecting a different action type.
[*] Fixed an issue where the NPC pane would scroll back to the top when some properties were edited.
[*] Entities that have been set to Stop on collision will disable any movement AI after a collision occurs.
[*] Added events for entities being Enabled and Disabled.
[*] The DestroySelf option on a Trigger will destroy the correct entity.
[*] Audio tracks can be deleted from the HUD pop-ups.
[*] The weapon clip can be set to refill when the player loses a life.
[*] Added an option for continuing a game where the player left off.  This resets the player's lives and score.
[*] Bullets use swept collision detection for improved accuracy at high speed.
[*] PlayerDef upgrades can be stacked so that the effect of one upgrade can be added to by another.
[*] Front-End items can be restricted to specific players.
[*] Fixed a problem with selecting User Variables in the front-end after deleting a User Variable in the Behaviour Editor.
[*] Fixed a problem where player entities are always enabled at the start of a game.
[*] Front-End items are navigable using player input controls and Fire 2 to select.
[*] Dialog windows are resizable.  Some other styles of window will be resizable in the next release.
[*] The Custom 5 collision group now works correctly.
[*] Added titles to many of the dialog windows to help usability.
[*] Increased the spacing on lists.
[*] Added section headers to some lists.
[*] Added a Help button to open the user guide.
[/list]

We've got a lot of feedback saying the Shoot 'Em Up Kit needs more tutorials.  We've been working on a Wiki, which is still in-progress and will be available soon.  Our intention is to build a tutorial tree within the Wiki to guide people through the features. We are also finishing a system to speed-up the creation of video tutorials and allow them to be quickly replaced as the user-interface evolves.

We have started to include some of the suggestions people have kindly made about the user interface, and this is our main focus for the next few weeks.  We're including in-editor tutorials; tool-tip help for all parameters; selection dialogs will show video examples; the user guide is being updated; and much more.  We know people are waiting for these and so we will release version 2.0.14 as soon as these are ready.

We'd hoped to have the template games ready for this release but we're simplifying map items first.  By default they will be clones of the Entity and so entire waves of ships, or sections of map, can be changed quickly and easily.  It also simplified the user-interface.  We're sorry this feature didn't make it in but it will be coming very soon.

It has been exciting to see some of the community showing off the games they have created at events around the world, and also products appearing on GreenLight and now Early Access.  We've also enjoyed taking part in Game Jams using the Shoot 'Em Up Kit.  It's a fun and useful way of testing the Kit.

We thank you again for supporting us as we develop the Shoot 'Em Up Kit.  As always, your comments and suggestions are very welcome; and if you encounter any problems then please let us know and we'll do our best to fix them as quickly as possible.

Thanks again

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit 2.0.12
notes.content:
We're pleased to announce that the latest update to the Shoot 'Em Up Kit is now available.

The change list for 2.0.12 is as follows:
[list]
[*]Effects can now be used to change sprites.
[*]Added a CRT/ScanLine post-processing effect option.
[*]Entities can automatically be enabled when they appear on-screen.
[*]Improved the formatting of the Property page for instanced entities.
[*]Fixed a directory warning when copying a project.
[*]Fixed an internal memory leak with the particle system.
[*]Fixed an issue that could prevent an Entity's 'destroy self' action from functioning properly.
[*]Fixed some issues with Bullet bouncing.
[*]NPC Generators and Splines can be deleted using the toolbar [Delete] button.
[*]The particle effect when a bullet is destroyed is now played at the front of the bullet.
[*]Fixed an issue that prevented a particle effect from playing when the player collects an Upgrade if the Upgrade duration was 0.0.
[*]The audio repeat time now works correctly.
[*]Sprites and Upgrades from Effects added in the Level Editor are now being added to package.
[*]Turn 90/180/270 has been replaced with Turn Yaw 90/180/270 and Turn Pitch 90/180/270.
[*]Fixed an issue that could create an extra sprite instance when adding a NPC Generator node after copying a Sprite.
[*]Fixed the default AI weighting for formations which was incorrectly set to zero.
[*]Fixed an issue that could prevent particle systems from being played after a period of time.
[*]NPCs are now correctly disabled when off-screen, if the option is set.
[*]The AI type 'MoveDirection' has been enabled again.
[*]Added Current Level Name to the Game properties.
[*]Triggers only activate HUD pop-ups when an Entity first enters (or re-enters) the area.
[*]Memory optimisations.
[*]Improvements to object cloning.
[*]When deleting an entity, a warning message is displayed if the entity is still referred to by another object
[*]Improved mouse controls.  It works best with the Acceleration types 'None Proportional' and 'Linear Proportional'.
[*]Sprite billboards work correctly in-game.
[*]Triggers are now shown when testing a game with the debug option.
[*]Added a delete button to remove music on the Front-End pages.
[*]Light orientation now works correctly when parented to an object tag.
[*]Video thumbnail icons are now created properly.
[*]Background videos are shown full-screen and the scale and rotation properties have been removed.
[*]Sprites default to firing in 2D axis.
[*]NPCs created by an NPC Generator can use bullet patterns.
[*]NPCs created by an NPC Generator use the activate when on-screen and deactivate when off-screen settings.
[*]Objects can now be seen much further from the camera.
[*]The copy button works correctly on the Upgrade Definition list.
[*]The definition list can be dragged around the screen.  It will be centred when re-opened.
[*]Fixed an issue that prevented upgrades triggered by a Damaged event from deactivating after their time had expired.
[*]The Bullet Red and Bullet Orange definitions have the correct damage multiplier (1.0).
[*]The Bullet Pattern definition has the correct Minimum Time (0.2).
[*]Fixed an issue that prevented the rate of fire from being adjusted on NPC Generator characters.
[*]Weapons are reloaded when a level restarts.
[*]Disabled weapons are correctly applied to NPC Generated characters.
[*]Some improvements to audio streaming.
[*]Minor user interface fixes.
[*]Stability fixes.
[/list]

There has been a lot of work behind the scenes on the Shoot 'Em Up Kit to position it for moving forward.  We will soon be introducing lots of optimisations, support for other graphics SDKs and improvements to the user interface.  We're also getting ready for the multi-platform version.

We'll soon be launching our wiki; as well as new features such as template games and an improved shield system.

We'd like to take this opportunity to thank everyone who has shared their feedback with us.  Your comments are always appreciated and really help to improve the Shoot 'Em Up Kit.

We hope you enjoy this new version.

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit 2.0.9
notes.content:
We are pleased to announce that version 2.0.9 of the Shoot 'Em Up Kit has been released.  This new version contains lots of features requested on the forums; as well as bug fixes and improvements.

The release notes since our last announcement (version 2.0.5) are as follows:
[b]Version 2.0.9[/b]
[list][*] Fixed some issues with the rotation of child items (Items that have a Parent Entity).
[*] Fixed some issues with the rotation of Effect particles.
[*] Player Entities set to reset '2 seconds ago' now spawn correctly when testing the game.
[*] Enemy Waves are correctly reset after a Player loses a life.
[*] Increased zoom in/out speed in Particle Editor.  The [Shift] keys will double the zoom speed while the [Control] keys will halve it.
[*] Fixed an issue with saving Front-End pages.
[*] Fixed an issue where selecting a Bullet Particle would set the Bullet Killed Particle instead.
[*] Automatic error reporting now occurs via Steam servers.
[*] Light direction settings are now saved correctly again.
[*] Fixed a problem with lighting from all levels being applied to each scene.
[*] Fixed a potential crash when lights are parented to items.
[*] Fixed an issue that could prevent Gravity and item parents from being set for the correct level in a multi-level game.
[*] Added some optimisations to the lighting system.
[*] Fixed a potential crash when switching between HUD Editor and testing the game.
[*] HUD sprites can now be scaled when using data values.
[*] Renamed some of the steps in the New Game Wizard.
[*] It is now possible to select the 'Thrust' control option in the New Game Wizard.
[*] Thrust and Shield effects now stop correctly when the Thrust/Shield button is released.
[*] Fixed an issue which could prevent Wave data from being transferred when copying levels.
[*] Added a fix which would read data if a level file became corrupt due to a failed level copy.
[*] Effects can be used to change the current Sprite.
[*] Added a new effect which is triggered when an Entity reaches the boundary of its Active Area.
[*] HUD, Front-End and Behaviour Editor data now works correctly with new Properties.  We apologise for the Score and Lives properties appearing incorrectly in the HUD after update 2.0.5.
[*] Added an option to allow NPC's to check whether they will shoot a teammate if they fire.  This has always been a hidden property which was set to 'On' but can now be turned off.
[*] Background sprites larger than the screen size can now be wrapped using the Level Editor's 'Movement' properties.
[*] Full-Screen games now use Vertical Sync (VSync).
[*] Sprites are scaled correctly in the Preview window.
[*] Fixed an issue with scrollbars not scrolling to the very bottom of a Window in specific circumstances.
[*] Fixed a potential crash when entering text in the Front-End Editor.
[*] Building a stand-alone package is now functional.  There may still be some issues and these will be addressed in subsequent builds.
[*] The 'Hidden' property for Entities is now saved correctly.
[/list]

We are currently improving the level editor by making it easier to replace Entities; Clone items; Select multiple-items; and build levels by dragging from a palette of objects.  We will then be creating template games to make it faster and easier to get a fully-featured game up and running.

We are also continuing to improve the documentation and create more tutorial videos.

Thank you for all your support.

notes.title: Shoot 'Em Up Kit 2.0.5
notes.content:
We are pleased to announce a new update to the Shoot 'Em Up Kit.  The new version includes new features such as air resistance, hidden objects, and more control of weapons.  There are also many fixes and improvements.

The release notes are:
[list]
[*] Player and NPC Entities use 'Stop' as their default Area Action.
[*] Added 'Resistance' property to simulate the slow down that occurs from the environment (e.g. Friction or Air-Resistance).
[*] Added 'Hidden' property to allow objects to be active yet invisible.
[*] Deleting a Sprite or Entity no longer returns to the top of the asset list.
[*] NPC Generators now place Sprite Entities in the same way as they do Mesh Entities.
[*] Fixed an issue with sprites not animating correctly in-game.
[*] The Sprite 'Loop' option is now saved correctly.
[*] Fixed an issue where an extra Entity could be created when using the Sprite Editor's 'Auto Build' option.
[*] The Max Duration property for Bullet Patterns now applies to both Player and NPC entities.
[*] If a CameraShot is set to move along a spline then setting the Tracking Style to 'Static' will make the camera's focus follow the spline too.
[*] Improved the way the Camera follows a spline.  The speed is consistent with Player and NPC units of measurement.
[*] Strafe Up and Strafe Down are now fully implemented.
[*] Chamber Time has been renamed Rate of Fire and is no longer part of the 'Reload' properties.
[*] Setting 'Num Bullets to Fire' to 0 will fire unlimited bullets.
[*] Setting 'Max Bullets' to 0 indicates there is no limit to the number of active bullets.
[*] Pop-Ups can now play audio effects.
[*] Fixed a problem with texture thumbnails not being displayed until you changed them.
[*] Fixed an issue which could display a sprite 1 pixel out in the x and y directions on the Sprite Preview window.
[*] The scrollbar no longer resets to the top of the pane when changing NPC properties.
[*] Fixed an issue with the project directory being reset when modifying other properties on the Settings menu.
[*] The 'Min Duration' and 'Max Duration' properties for Bullet Patterns now work correctly for the Player.
[*] Added fixes and safety checks to improve stability.
[/list]
Thank you for all the feedback.  We hope you enjoy this new version.
